entities.summary: Publius Juventius Celsus was a renowned ancient Roman jurist, born into a family of jurists, and the son of a jurist of the same name. He was influential in shaping the High Classical era's juridical landscape alongside Julian. Celsus Titus Aufidius Hoenius Severianus was the son of a little-known jurist, and his significance lies in his contributions to Roman law. His work had a lasting impact on the development of Roman law and its influence can be seen in the Justinian Code. The jurist's family background and his own work demonstrate the importance of jurists in the evolution of Roman law. Celsus's legacy is a testament to the significance of the High Classical era in Roman history. The jurist's work is an enduring example of the impact of individual scholars on the development of their field.
